verdict.rationale: Cua Driver documents a 'Set permissions' control over what the agent may do. Spaces lock credential and app items until the operator approves unattended access, require Touch ID for sensitive items, and check the app bundle's SHA-256 before opening it, which points to enforced gating of accounts and apps. However, the permissions feature appears only as a one-line heading, with no detail on per-app or per-surface allowlists or on how they are enforced. Missing for 10: documented per-app/surface allowlist semantics, explicit statement of enforcement versus advisory behavior for Driver permissions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an operator, I can limit which apps, surfaces, or accounts the agent may touch, and the limit is enforced, not advisory

citations.quote: Control what the agent may do — Set permissions
Every item is locked until you allow unattended access. Approve requests, lock or delete items
Nothing is read until you approve, and sensitive items need Touch ID. The Space checks the bundle's SHA-256 before it opens the app.
